# Psalm 105 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** Give thanks to the LORD! Call out his name! Tell the nations what he has done!

**2** Sing to him! Make music for him! Talk about all his incredible miracles!

**3** Take pride in his holy name! Let the hearts of those who seek the LORD be filled with joy!

**4** Look to the LORD for strength! Seek his presence constantly!

**5** Remember the miracles he performed, the wonders and the verdicts he pronounced —

**6** you descendants of his servant Abraham, you children of Jacob, his chosen people!

**7** He is the LORD our God! His justice reaches every corner of the earth.

**8** He remembers his covenant forever — the promise he made for a thousand generations,

**9** the agreement he made with Abraham, the oath he swore to Isaac,

**10** the decree he confirmed to Jacob, the permanent covenant with Israel:

**11** 'I will give you the land of Canaan as your personal inheritance.'

**12** Back when they were just a handful of people — so few! — and strangers in the land,

**13** wandering from one nation to another, from one kingdom to the next,

**14** he didn't let anyone push them around. He confronted kings for their sake:

**15** 'Don't lay a finger on my chosen ones! Don't harm my prophets!'

**16** Then he called down a famine on the land and cut off every source of food.

**17** But he had already sent someone ahead of them — Joseph, sold as a slave.

**18** They clamped his feet in chains; an iron collar went around his neck.

**19** Until his prediction came true, the LORD's word tested and refined him.

**20** The king sent for him and set him free; the ruler of nations released him.

**21** He put him in charge of the entire royal household, ruler over everything the king owned,

**22** with authority over the king's officials and wisdom to teach the elders.

**23** Then Israel came to Egypt; Jacob settled in the land of Ham.

**24** God made his people incredibly fruitful — more powerful than their enemies.

**25** He changed the Egyptians' hearts so they hated his people and plotted against his servants.

**26** Then he sent Moses, his servant, and Aaron, his chosen one.

**27** They performed God's miraculous signs among the Egyptians — wonders in the land of Ham.

**28** God sent darkness and made the land pitch black; they did not resist his commands.

**29** He turned their water into blood and killed all their fish.

**30** Frogs overran the country — even the king's private rooms!

**31** He gave the order and swarms of flies invaded, along with gnats across the whole territory.

**32** Instead of rain he sent hail — and lightning bolts streaking through the land.

**33** He destroyed their grapevines and fig trees; he shattered every tree in the country.

**34** He spoke, and locusts came — young locusts beyond counting —

**35** and they devoured every plant in the land, eating every crop from the ground.

**36** Then he struck down every firstborn in the land — the pride and joy of every family.

**37** He led Israel out loaded with silver and gold, and not one person among them stumbled.

**38** Egypt was relieved to see them go, because they had become terrified of Israel.

**39** God spread out a cloud as a canopy over them and provided fire to light up the night.

**40** The people asked, and he sent quail. He satisfied them with bread from heaven.

**41** He split the rock open and water poured out — it flowed through the desert like a river!

**42** He did all this because he remembered his sacred promise to his servant Abraham.

**43** So he brought his people out with joy — his chosen ones with shouts of happiness!

**44** He gave them the lands of other nations; they inherited what other peoples had worked for —

**45** all so that they would follow his instructions and obey his laws. Hallelujah!

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **105:16-22**: The Joseph story in six verses — from slave to ruler. What looked like tragedy was actually God positioning someone to save the family. The psalm sees divine chess moves where Joseph saw prison walls.

- **105:42-45**: The punchline of the whole psalm: God did all of this because he remembered his promise. Everything — the plagues, the Exodus, the wilderness, the conquest — flows from one act of divine memory.

— PNEUMA
